title: How rare is a 100% black cat?
content:
The cat, also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small carnivorous mammal. It is an obligate carnivore, requiring a predominantly meat-based diet. Its retractable claws are adapted to killing small prey species such as mice and rats.
Domestic cats are characterized by retractable claws, powerful bodies, acute senses, long tails, and specialized teeth adapted for hunting prey.

Black cats are as fascinating as they are adorable—which is saying a lot. On top of being fun and cute, they’ve also captivated cultures all over the world throughout history.

One in 22. There are as many as 22 recognised breeds that can have solid black colouring but the only all-black feline is the Bombay cat.

The breed was developed in the 1950s by crossing Sable Burmese with black American Shorthairs with the aim to create a cat that resembled a miniature black panther.

title: Are Bengal kitties good house pets?
content:
Веngаlѕ аrе vеrу еntеrtаіnіng аnd аffесtіоnаtе. Тhеу mаkе grеаt реtѕ, but уоu muѕt bе рrераrеd fоr thеіr рlауful реrѕоnаlіtу аnd іnсrеdіblе іntеllіgеnсе. Lіkе thеіr аnсеѕtоrѕ, thеѕе саtѕ аrе vеrу асtіvе сrеаturеѕ. Тhеу аrе еnеrgеtіс аnd rеquіrе еntеrtаіnmеnt. Іf саtѕ dо nоt gеt thе асtіоn thеу nееd, thеу mау dаmаgе hоuѕеhоld іtеmѕ аnd furnіturе.

А Веngаl саt іn thе hаndѕ оf hеr оwnеr, lеttіng thе оwnеr реt hеr tummу.Веngаlѕ аrе аlѕо knоwn аѕ аvіd thіеvеѕ. Тhеу оftеn ѕtеаl аnd hіdе іntrіguіng іtеmѕ (е.g., јеwеlrу, соіnѕ, kеуѕ) аnd lоvе ѕрlаѕhіng іn thе wаtеr аnd рlауіng wіth рареr, ѕо kеер іmроrtаnt dосumеntѕ lосkеd аnd оffеr lоtѕ оf tоуѕ tо kеер thеm buѕу.

Оvеrаll, Веngаl саtѕ аrе соnfіdеnt, сurіоuѕ, аnd hарру. Тhеу аrе nо mоrе аggrеѕѕіvе thаn thе аvеrаgе dоmеѕtіс саt, аnd, аѕ wіth аll саtѕ, thеіr tеmреrаmеnt саn bе mоldеd wіth trаіnіng. Тhеу аrе аlѕо frіеndlу аnd lоvіng, аnd іt’ѕ nоt unuѕuаl fоr thеm tо dеvеlор grеаt lоуаltу tо а ѕіnglе fаmіlу mеmbеr. 

The Bengal is a sleek, muscular cat with a wild appearance, enhanced by the bold marbling and spotting on their thick, luxurious coat. Despite their striking appearance, physically there is nothing extreme about their build or structure, as this is a well-balanced cat without any exaggerated features, smallish ears, wedge shaped head, neat paws and athletic outline. 

Lifespan: 10 - 16 years
Weight: 3.6 - 7.7kg
Colours: Bengal cats come in come with a spotted marble coat in brown, silver and snow.

The first Bengal cat was born in the early 1960s when a domestic cat mated with an Asian leopard cat. Most of today’s Bengals can trace their lineage to the 1980s when breeding began in earnest.

title: The cougar, also called puma
content:
A cougar (Puma concolor) is a large, solitary wild cat also known as a mountain lion, puma, or panther, famous for its wide range across the Americas, powerful leaps, and tawny coat with a black-tipped tail, serving as a crucial predator that regulates prey populations in healthy ecosystems. Beyond the animal, "cougar" is slang for an older woman dating younger men (though debated) and also refers to a type of U.S. military armored vehicle. 

Cougars are quite large, with the males typically weighing between 120 and 160 pounds and the females about 75 and 110 pounds. Both male and female cougars will grow to approximately 5-6 feet in length. That’s the length of a twin or full-size mattress! Imagine a carnivorous cougar stretching out alongside your bed! Cougars are interesting because they resemble the typical domestic cat, but they are much more threatening.

Cougars are adaptable to many different types of climates, as they can be found in forests, deserts, swamps, and mountains. This breed is known to travel long distances, often up to 600 miles, so they’re likely to see many different environments. Cougars communicate by mewing, hissing, growling, and purring. 

Unlike many other animals, cougars typically depend on sight more than smell when hunting prey. Common prey includes sheep, horses, cattle, and insects. However, deer typically make up a majority of their diet. The cougar hunts by stalking and then finding an opportunity to ambush its prey. This breed lives for about 10 years in the wild and 20 years in captivity. 

The Animal: Puma concolor
    • Names: Has more names than any other mammal (cougar, puma, mountain lion, catamount, panther).
    • Description: Large, muscular cat; typically reddish-brown to gray, with a long tail, powerful hind legs for jumping (up to 40 ft horizontally). Kittens are spotted.
    • Habitat & Range: Widest range of any wild terrestrial mammal in the Western Hemisphere, from Canada to South America, in forests, canyons, and mountains.
  • Diet: Carnivores, primarily eating deer, helping control herbivore populations.
  • Behavior: Solitary, secretive, excellent hunters; avoid humans but encounters increase as habitats overlap.

title: How do butterflies eat?
content:
Butterflies don’t eat. They drink! They use their mouth, called a proboscis, like a straw to sip their food. When they’re not drinking, they roll their tongue up and tuck it under their chin.

Butterflies eat by sipping liquids with their unique, straw-like mouthpart called a proboscis, which uncoils to drink nectar from flowers, juice from rotting fruits, and even water or minerals from damp soil (puddling).

They can't chew, so their diet is entirely liquid, using suction to pull fluids up the hollow proboscis, which coils neatly under their chin when not in use.

title: Does a polar bear have a strong sense of smell?
content:
Polar bears have a keen sense of smell, which they use to find prey. A polar bear can sniff out a seal on the ice 20 miles (32 kilometers) away, and can smell a seal's breathing hole in the ice more than half a mile away, according to the National Zoo.

Their sense of smell is highly developed, enabling them to: 

  • Detect a seal on the ice from up to 20 miles (32 kilometers) away.
  • Smell a seal's breathing hole from over half a mile (around 1 km) away, even if it is under a meter of compacted snow or ice.
  • Locate mates and avoid rivals by following distinct scents left by other bears on the ice.
  • Find carcasses from long distances, acting as opportunistic scavengers when necessary.

An adult male polar bear typically weighs between 775 and 1,200 pounds (351 to 544 kilograms), or the weight of about five to seven men. The largest polar bear ever recorded was a male weighing 2,209 pounds (1,000 kg), according to Polar Bear International. By contrast, adult females weigh only half as much as males, or 330 to 650 pounds (50 to 295 kg).

The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed. The polar bear is the largest extant species of bear and land carnivore by body mass, with adult males weighing 300–800 kg.

title: Why don't polar bears slip on the ice?
content:
The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed. The polar bear is the largest extant species of bear and land carnivore by body mass, with adult males weighing 300–800 kg.

In order to walk easily on the icy terrain polar bears have non-retractable claws and paw pads that act like suction cups, thanks to the presence of small bumps called papillae. Their huge paws can up to 30cm across, which help them walk on thin ice.

Polar bears don't slip on ice because

their huge paws have rough, bumpy pads (papillae) and fur between their toes for grip, plus non-retractable claws for traction, acting like natural snowshoes and cleats, while their oily fur repels ice, preventing it from sticking and making them more agile on the icy terrain. 

Paw Features for Grip
  • Papillae: Their black paw pads have tiny, tall bumps (papillae) that create friction and grip against ice and snow, similar to suction cups.
  • Fur: Shaggy fur between their toes and on the pads provides extra insulation and helps with purchase on the slippery surfaces.
  • Claws: Thick, curved, non-retractable claws dig in for traction, helping them hold onto prey and keep their footing.
  • Size: Their large, wide paws distribute weight, acting like snowshoes to prevent sinking in snow and providing stability. 

Polar bears live in the Arctic regions of North America, Europe, and Asia, primarily on sea ice, but also on land in countries like Canada, Russia, Alaska (USA), Greenland, and Norway (Svalbard), following the ice where they hunt seals, their main food source. They are marine mammals, spending most of their lives on the ice, though they can swim long distances and den on land to give birth.

title: Why polar bears are so important?
content:
The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed. The polar bear is the largest extant species of bear and land carnivore by body mass, with adult males weighing 300–800 kg.

Polar bears have a strong cultural significance for Arctic people, and beyond, polar bears are top predators in their food web. Which means they play a vital role in the balance of their ecosystem.

By helping protect the polar bear, we’re helping to make sure the Arctic food chain stays healthy, for the benefit of wildlife and people in and beyond the Arctic. The Arctic provides fish for millions of people, including here in the UK.

Ecological Importance

  • Keystone Species: As top predators, they regulate seal numbers, preventing overgrazing of marine life like crustaceans and fish, which supports the entire food web.
  • Food Source for Scavengers: Polar bears drag seal carcasses onto the ice, providing critical energy and nutrients for scavengers like Arctic foxes, gulls, and wolves.
  • Indicator of Environmental Health: Their health reflects the health of the Arctic environment; struggling polar bears signal broader ecosystem distress, which impacts global climate. 
Cultural & Human Importance
  • Indigenous Culture: Polar bears are deeply tied to the identity, traditions, and survival of Arctic Indigenous peoples who rely on the land and sea.
  • Economic Value: In places like Churchill, Canada, polar bears drive wildlife tourism, supporting local economies.
  • Global Symbol: They are a powerful symbol of the Arctic and the impacts of climate change, urging global action to protect the planet.

Polar bears live in the Arctic regions of North America, Europe, and Asia, primarily on sea ice, but also on land in countries like Canada, Russia, Alaska (USA), Greenland, and Norway (Svalbard), following the ice where they hunt seals, their main food source. They are marine mammals, spending most of their lives on the ice, though they can swim long distances and den on land to give birth.

title: What is the largest snake ever found?
content:
The northern green anaconda (Eunectes akayima) is considered the largest living snake by weight, while the reticulated python (Malayopython reticulatus) is the longest. The extinct Titanoboa and Vasuki Indicus remain the largest snakes in history, though which one was the absolute largest is debated. 

Largest Snakes by Category
  • Heaviest Living Snake: The newly identified northern green anaconda (Eunectes akayima) holds the title for the heaviest living snake species, with specimens potentially exceeding 500 kg (1,100 lbs). Previously, this title was held by the southern green anaconda (Eunectes murinus), which can weigh over 200 kg (440 lbs).
  • Longest Living Snake: The reticulated python (Malayopython reticulatus) is the longest snake species, with the longest unverified historical record at 10 m (33 ft) and reliable scientific reports of individuals up to about 7.67 m (25.2 ft).
  • Largest Extinct Snake: The extinct Titanoboa cerrejonensis is generally considered the largest snake in history, estimated to have been around 13 meters (42 feet) long and weighing over a ton. A recently discovered ancient snake, Vasuki Indicus, suggests even bigger prehistoric relatives, though current estimates place it as potentially longer in maximum length but comparable in overall size to Titanoboa.

title: What is the no. 1 cutest dog?
content:
Golden Retriever.

Known for their gentle nature and endless affection, Golden Retrievers are one of the cutest dog breeds and a family favourite worldwide. They are intelligent, loyal, easy to train, patient, and perfect companions for both kids and adults.

It's safe to say that this breed is one of the most personable around. Golden Retrievers are always eager to please and have a calm temperament, which means they will be happy to socialise with everyone – even with other pets!

The Golden Retriever is a Scottish breed of retriever dog of medium-large size. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat. It is a working dog, and registration is subject to successful completion of a working trial. It is commonly kept as a companion dog and is among the most frequently registered breeds in several Western countries; some may compete in dog shows or obedience trials, or work as guide dogs.

title: Fun Facts About Seals
content:
Seals are found along most coasts and cold waters, but a majority of them live in the Arctic and Antarctic waters. Harbor, ringed, ribbon, spotted, and bearded seals, as well as northern fur seals and Steller sea lions, live in the Arctic region.

Seals are marine mammals who can be found in different oceans around the world. Habitats vary depending on the species of seal.

Seals have developed lots of different adaptations that help them survive and thrive in their marine habitats.

Seals have several natural predators. This depends on the type of seal and the habitat it lives in. Here are the main predators of seals.

March 22 marks International Seal Day, a day the whole world should celebrate in earnest! To mark this momentous occasion – which should really see us all laze about in the sun, feeding on sumptuous sardines

1. Seals Are Part of the Pinniped Order of Marine Mammals

The pinniped order of marine mammals also includes sea lions, walruses and fur seals. There are 33 species of pinnipeds in the world and all are believed to have evolved from once terrestrial otter-like creatures.

2. Seals Prefer Cold Sea Waters

Cold sea waters are primarily found in the Arctic and Antarctic regions. There are four ice specialized species breeding on the Antarctic ice, the Leopard seals, Ross seals, Weddell seals, and Crabeater seals.

3. In the Wild, Grey Seals Can Live for Up to 35 Years

Female seals are boasting a higher life expectancy than male seals. Female seals can get up to 30 years old in the wild, while male seals rarely reach the age of 25.

4. Seal Species Come in Different Sizes

The smallest seal species is the Galapagos Fur Seal (1m in length and 45kg in weight) whilst the largest is the Southern Elephant Seal which weighs a whopping 3,850kgs and measures up to 5m in length!

5. Some Seal Species Feed off Fellow Seals!

Some seal species, like the Leopard Seal, feed off fellow seals! Most, however, feed off crustaceans, fish and seabirds (if they can catch them).

6. The Crabeater Seal Boasts the Largest Population of All the Seal Species

The Crabeater Seal can be spotted on an Antarctic cruise. Estimates put their numbers at between 2 and 75 million individuals, worldwide. As cute and friendly as they may look, seals can actually be fervently territorial and quite aggressive.

7. Seals Can Sleep Underwater

Seals usually only come on land to escape predators like whales and sharks, as well as to mate, give birth, feed and moult.

8. Some Seals Can Dive Up to 900m in Depth

Seal will dive up to 900m in search for food. Some seals can hold their breath underwater for up to 2 hours! The Northern Elephant seals spend the majority of their time at depth. They are only coming to the surface for a few minutes between dives. Before the dive, the Elephant seal first exhales to empty their lungs. During their long migration trek, these creatures dive for food in this manner.

9. A Seal Mum’s Milk Can Be Up to 50% Fat

Because of the high fat rate, seal pups can put on 2kgs a DAY. That should make you feel a little better about your Christmas and New Year calorific splurge!

10. Over the Last Century, Various Species Have Gone Extinct

Seals have been hunted throughout history, with their fat and fur being highly coveted. Although a great majority of species are not endangered – the Galapagos Fur Seal is one of the exceptions – seals are still a highly protected mammal in most parts of the world. Over the last century, various species have gone extinct, including the Caribbean Monk Seal and Japanese Sea Lion.

11. Earless Seals Do Have Ears

Earless seals are one of the main mammalian groups in the pinniped seal lineage. Other than their name would tell you, earless seals do have ears. Their ears are covered beneath their skin. So they do have ears, but you just can’t see them.

12. Seals Can Be Hooligans

In Gisborne, New Zealand, a resident elephant seal, named Homer, had an infamous reputation for hooliganism. He used to routinely overturn parked cars in town and once even knocked over a restaurant’s power supply box. Experts believed that Homer’s energetic ‘rubbings’ were actually ever-so-slightly misguided sexual advances.

13. Seals Boast a Gestation Period of About 11 Months

The longest pregnancy in the pinniped family belongs to the walrus, which is pregnant for about 16 months.

14. Mother and Baby Seals Recognise Each Other

One of our really lovely fun facts about seals is that mother and baby seals recognise each other through a familiar call. A study in Alaska found that mum-bub recognition was possible even after a 4-year long separation.

15. Alpha-Male Elephant Seals Are Quite the Possessive Don Juans

A study in the Falkland Islands proved that alpha-male Elephant Seals are quite the possessive Don Juans In one colony alone, over 92% of pups born at any given time were fathered by the group’s alpha-male alone and up to 72% of all other males in the colony, had NEVER been observed mating at all.

title: Amazing Facts about Giant Sequoia Trees
content:
The giant sequoia is a huge evergreen tree. It grows only on the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada mountains in the U.S. state of California. Its scientific name is Sequoiadendron giganteum. It is related to the redwood.

  • Several different living sequoia specimens hold different world tree records for size, volume and lifespan.
  • A giant sequoia located in the Sequoia National Forest, California, United States is considered the sixth tallest living tree in the world. The last time it was measured it had a height of 314 feet.
  • A giant sequoia tree known as General Sherman is considered the largest living tree by volume. It’s located in the Sequoia National Forest, California, United States and has an estimated trunk volume of 52,500 cubic feet.
  • A giant sequoia known as General Grant has the fourth largest trunk diameter in the world. It’s located in General Grant Grove, California, United States and has a trunk diameter of 29 feet.
  • A giant sequoia known only as CBR26 is the fourth oldest tree in the world. Before it died, it was in Sierra Nevada, California, United States and had an estimated age of 3,649 years.
  • Giant sequoia trees have evolved to resist and actual benefit from forest fires.
  • The bark of a giant sequoia tree prevents any significant damage from a forest fire. It’s thickness and composition insulate it from the heat of a fire.
  • The seed cones produced by giant sequoias are activated by a fire. The heat from a forest fire will dry out the cones and, in a week, or two release its seeds. Since the fire will have cleared the soil of all vegetation it gives the seeds the best chance to germinate and grow.

The giant sequoia is so large that it is sometimes called simply the big tree. Some giant sequoias are more than 280 feet (85 meters) tall. They have huge trunks that are sometimes more than 100 feet (30 meters) around at the bottom. The reddish brown bark can grow to more than 12 inches (30 centimeters) thick. Giant sequoias usually have branches only near the top because the lower branches fall away as the tree grows. The leaves are blue-green.

The giant sequoia is a conifer, which means that it produces cones that hold its seeds. At 3.5 inches (9 centimeters) long, the cones are tiny compared to the tree.

Giant sequoias can live to a very old age. Some are more than 3,500 years old. The wood is rich in chemicals that keep away insect pests and prevent rotting. The thick bark does not burn easily and helps to protect the tree from fire.

title: Incredible Coyote Facts!
content:
Coyotes are members of the dog family, also known as Canidae. Canis latrans, more commonly known as coyotes, are wild members of the dog family. They are known for being highly clever and savvy animals. They live in North and Central America, today, anywhere from California to Alaska, although they used to live in Western America and Mexico. 

  • Alternate names for this species include the prairie wolf and the brush wolf.
  • The coyote was an important figure in North American folklore. It was often viewed as a symbol of craftiness and deceit, sometimes donning various guises to trick people. In Mesoamerica, it was a cosmological symbol of military strength.
  • Coyotes are incredibly mobile animals that will roam around their natural territory for several miles every day. If they are facing stiff competition for food and resources, then it may travel more than a hundred miles in search of a new home.
  • Coyotes are animals that are agile on both land and water, but they are relatively poor climbers.

Coyotes once lived primarily in open prairies and deserts, but they now roam American forests and mountains. The range of a coyote habitat is big, and they even live in cities, such as Los Angeles. They can also be found in Mexico and Central America

The fact coyotes can adapt to live in such a variety of different habitats shows how intelligent they are! They thrive living in outdoor open spaces as well as busy urban locations, which differs to a lot of other animals.

Coyotes live in dens. Sometimes they dig these themselves, and other times they find another animal's den and make it bigger to suit themselves! They also used crevices in rocks and hollowed out trees to make a den. Usually they dig a tunnel under the ground and, at the end of it, they'll dig a larger area where they'll sleep. It's also where their babies will stay until they're old enough to venture outside. The den will sometimes have two entrances; one of which will be hidden. Some coyotes will even have more than one den. This is so they can hide if an enemy finds one!

They're mammals that eat both vegetation and meat, which means they are called omnivores. Coyotes aren't particularly fussy eaters - they're willing to eat anything, even garbage! They'll typically eat vegetables, fruits, grasses, voles, mice, lizards, birds, deer and snakes. Coyotes are also carrion eaters, as they'll eat dead animals if given the opportunity.

The coyote is characterised by its long, coarse, greyish-brown fur with a lighter underside, as well as a bushy tail, erect and pointed ears, and a long, slender snout. Compared to wolves, coyotes are medium-sized canids with a smaller size and lighter build. A coyote is typically around 60 centimetres (2 feet) tall and up to 1.3 metres (3.3-4.2 feet) long, including a 30- to 40-centimetre (11- to 15-inch) tail. Coyotes’ size and colour can vary depending on the region in which they live. They can weigh anywhere from nine to 23 kilograms (20 to 50 pounds), with the largest coyotes residing in the northeast US and eastern Canada.

Coyotes are proficient hunters. When they run, their tails point downwards, and they can reach speeds of up to 64 kilometres per hour (40 miles per hour).

title: Coyotes Are Smaller Than Wolves, Bigger Than Foxes
content:
Coyotes are members of the dog family, also known as Canidae.

Coyotes are indeed smaller than wolves but larger than foxes, sitting in the middle size-wise within the canid family, resembling a medium-sized dog (like a Border Collie) compared to bigger wolves and smaller, cat-sized foxes, with distinct features like coyotes' narrower snouts and pointed ears versus wolves' broader muzzles and foxes' bushy tails. 

Size & Build:
  • Coyotes: Weigh 20-50 lbs, about 2 feet tall at the shoulder, sleek build, narrow snout, pointed ears.
  • Wolves: Much larger, up to 100+ lbs, broad muzzle, shorter rounded ears, heavier build.
  • Foxes: Smallest, cat-sized, very pointed snout, bushy tail often with a white tip. 
Key Distinctions:
  • Snout: Coyotes (narrow/pointed) vs. Wolves (broad) vs. Foxes (tiny/pointed).
  • Ears: Coyotes (large & pointed) vs. Wolves (shorter & rounded).
  • Tail: Coyotes (bushy, hangs down) vs. Foxes (very bushy, almost body-length).
  • Social Behavior: Wolves live in packs; coyotes and foxes are more solitary or in pairs. 

Coyotes were originally found in arid areas of the US, Canada, and Mexico, within prairies, deserts, and open forests. However, coyotes have expanded their range due to a variety of factors, including human activity, habitat alteration, and a decline in the populations of their natural predators.

As highly adaptable creatures, coyotes are now widely distributed across North and Central America. They’ve even been observed near the border of South America. They live in coniferous and deciduous forests, grasslands and prairies, deserts, and urban and suburban areas.

They can weigh anywhere from nine to 23 kilograms (20 to 50 pounds), with the largest coyotes residing in the northeast US and eastern Canada.

title: How far do wolves travel?
content:
Wolves are the largest members of the dog family. Packs of gray wolves hunt at night, using their speed, sharp teeth and claws to catch caribou, moose, deer, bison, beavers, rabbits and fish.

Wolves are hunters, and they travel far and wide to locate prey. They may travel 50 miles or more each day in search of food, and they are superbly designed for a life on the move. Because their elbows turn inward, their lean bodies are precisely balanced over their large feet. With their long legs and ground-eating stride, they can travel tirelessly for hours on end, wasting no energy. Dispersing wolves, those leaving packs in search of their own mates, have been known to travel hundreds of miles away from their home territory. Satellite and Global Positioning System (GPS) collars allow researchers to document the remarkable travels of wolves.

title: Where do the biggest wolves live?
content:
In the Siberian tundra, the Alaskan tundra wolf (Canis lupus albus) reigns supreme. With an average weight range of 88 to 108 pounds (39.9 to 50 kg) and a length of up to 6 feet (1.8 meters) including the tail, these wolves are a force to be reckoned with in one of the harshest environments on Earth.

Their thick fur coats, ranging from white to grey, are not just stunning; they're vital for survival in the subzero temperatures they call home.

This wolf is a skilled hunter, seamlessly adapted to its freezing realm. Their diet is as diverse as the tundra itself, ranging from Siberian roe deer to wild boar, showcasing their prowess and adaptability in tracking and taking down a variety of prey.

Canada hosts the world's largest wolf population, with more than 50,000 wolves inhabiting its vast landscape. Wolves are heavily hunted and trapped throughout the country, however, and are often killed when they stray from the protection of national and provincial parks.

The gray wolf, also called the timber wolf, is the largest member of the canine family with fur ranging from gray to brown, black or white. Packs of gray wolves hunt at night, using their speed, sharp teeth and claws to catch caribou, moose, deer, bison, beavers, rabbits and fish.

From tundra to desert, Great Plains to temperate rainforest, wolves and their prey have adapted to a wide variety of climates and habitats. The largest concentrations of wolves now reside in the northern regions of the world such as Alaska, Canada and Russia.

Wolves are one of the most adaptable predators on the planet. One of the more fascinating wolf facts is that they’re capable of living in a wide range of habitats including:

  • Forests
  • Tundras
  • Grasslands
  • Deserts
  • Mountains

title: How are wolves different than dogs?
content:
Dogs are less fearful and more playful than their wolf cousins. Wolves have yellow eyes, whereas dogs more commonly have brown or blue eyes. Wolves are built to run with narrow chests and long legs, whereas the domestic dog tends to be wider and stockier. Dogs tend to be less mentally mature than a wolf of similar age.

The gray wolf, also called the timber wolf, is the largest member of the canine family with fur ranging from gray to brown, black or white. Packs of gray wolves hunt at night, using their speed, sharp teeth and claws to catch caribou, moose, deer, bison, beavers, rabbits and fish.

Both wolves and dogs have the same number of teeth, but they, along with the skull and jaw, are larger and stronger in the wolf. “This is likely due to their need to bite and break things like bones in the wild, compared with dogs who evolved much more as scavengers of human refuse,” says Dr. Hughes.

Despite being portrayed in some outlets as vicious, experts say that wolves are actually shy and will avoid people. It’s also incredibly rare that a wolf will attack a person.

title: How much does a hippo weigh?
content:

Hippos are recognisable for their barrel-shaped torsos, wide-opening mouths with large canine tusks, nearly hairless bodies, short legs, and large size.

title: Elephant brains grow almost as much as human brains after birth
content:
The scientists were also able to show that elephants exhibit very large postnatal brain growth. The brains of adult elephants are about three times as heavy as they were at birth. This means that elephants have a significantly higher lifetime brain growth than all primates – with the exception of humans, in which the brain at birth weighs only around a fifth of its final weight.

They have a developed cerebral cortex, which is the part of the brain that helps solve problems. They have a large hippocampus, which is linked to emotion, and is part of the reason elephants have been observed having significant emotional reactions to things, including suffering from PTSD.

Elephants are exceptionally smart creatures. They have the largest brain of any land animal, and three times as many neurons as humans. While many of these neurons exist to control the elephant’s large and dexterous body, these creatures have demonstrated their impressive mental capabilities time and time again.

Much like the rest of the elephant, their brains are huge. Weighing an average 4.8kg, the largest among living and extinct terrestrial animals.

The fact that elephant brains are well rounded and developed means they are able to display a wide range of behaviors including grief, learning, play, mimicry compassion and cooperation.

title: Tips for Dealing With Long Words
content:
Living with a social phobia, like a fear of long words, can feel isolating, but there are ways to cope. In addition to working alongside a licensed mental health professional to reduce anxiety, find activities that help bring you joy and decrease the severity of your symptoms.

Other techniques that can help you manage your fear of long words include:

  • Breaking big words into smaller components: When you come across a long word that you do not know, it can help to split it into smaller words. For example, the word pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis
  • can be broken into pneumon- (meaning lungs), ultra- (beyond), microscopic- silico- (referring to silicon), volcano-, coniosis (a lung condition caused by dust). 
  • Substituting shorter words: Replace long words with shorter ones. For example, use lab for laboratory, limo for limousine, max for maximum, fridge for refrigerator, and rehab for rehabilitation. 
  • Taking your time: If you begin to feel anxious when you encounter a long word, there is no need to rush. Pause, take a few deep breaths, then slowly read over the word, breaking it into smaller, digestible pieces.

title: What is the no. 1 deadliest snake in the world?
content: https://taronga.org.au/animals/inland-taipan
src:
The inland taipan (Oxyuranus microlepidotus), also commonly known as the western taipan, small-scaled snake, or fierce snake.

The title for "most dangerous" snake depends on the criteria, but the Inland Taipan (Fierce Snake) has the most toxic venom of any land snake, while the Saw-scaled Viper causes the most human deaths due to its aggression and habitat near people.

Also known as the Fierce Snake, this taipan is the world’s most venomous. Despite this reputation, humans are rarely bitten as the snake is both shy and found only in remote semi-arid areas.

Are Inland Taipans Threatened?

This species has disappeared from parts of its historic range, likely including NSW, however is currently classed as Least Concern. As mammal-specialists, taipans have been less affected by the spread of poisonous Cane Toads across Australia than other snakes. Their specialisation in mammals however makes them dependent on prey availability, which has been reduced in areas by cats and foxes. They have also been assessed as highly vulnerable to the future impacts of climate change on the Australian landscape.

title: Why is 95% of the universe invisible?
content:
95% of the Universe is made up of dark matter and dark energy. These are words astronomers have come up with to give a name to the mysterious, invisible side of the Universe.

The Universe isn't quite what we think it is - in fact, we can only see a tiny fraction of it.

For decades, physicists have been trying to analyse what this elusive, undetected part of our universe really is. What is dark matter? How can we find it, and what is it made of? After some serious digging, scientists have realised that dark matter is only a small part of the bigger story - just the start of it. There is also another component of the universe which we call dark energy. 

Dark matter makes up 25% of the 'unknown stuff' in the universe, and the other 70% is made up of 'dark energy.'

title: Does Celery Affect Weight?
content:

Celery is a low-calorie food that promotes weight loss by boosting metabolism, increasing fat burn, and prolonging satiety.

title: What Happens to Your Blood Pressure When You Drink Coconut Water Regularly?
content:
Coconut water in normal amounts is safe for most people.

  • Coconut water may lower BP in people with hypertension, but more research is needed.
  • Be mindful of minerals in coconut water, like potassium and sodium, particularly if you have a medical condition or take medications that may make your body less able to filter them out.
  • Research is limited, but coconut water has been studied for BP at 150 mL (about 5 ounces) daily.
